comparator.name: General Cultural Studies (Algemene Cultuurwetenschappen)
comparator.sourceNotes: The OU programme page confirms a 180-EC part-time Dutch-taught BA with a 60-EC propedeuse and 120-EC postpropedeuse, four main themes (Diversity and inclusion; Digital transitions in cultural heritage; Technology, media and culture; Stigma, health and culture) and no formal routes. The 2026-27 study guide (BD476) and annual schedule list the courses, each 5 EC unless stated: twelve propedeuse courses (introductory course, six thematic/portal-type courses, four method courses, Academic writing), four themed postpropedeuse course sets, further electives (Stage 10 EC, Onderzoeksontwikkelingen en -vaardigheden 10 EC), and a 15-EC Bachelor graduation trajectory or thesis practicum. The study guide's schematic table, however, gives component sizes (introduction 5, methods 4x = 20, portal courses 4x = 20, academic writing 5; theme blocks 45, choice block 30, free space 30, skills block 15, graduation 15) that sum to 185 EC rather than 180, with a 50-EC propedeuse against the stated 60, and the annual schedule lists six rather than four portal-type courses. The guide does not state which courses form each theme block or the skills block, and the 2026-27 programme-specific education and examination regulations that would settle these points could not be found; The original audit additionally located a programme-specific 2025–2026 OER (s4): 60 propedeuse + 45 theme study + 15 restricted choice + 30 free space + 15 skills + 15 graduation = 180. That is a coherent dated prior-year allocation, not proof of applicability to 2026–2027. It supersedes the overly broad claim that only the general OER exists. Fresh 2026–2027 guide retrieval on 2026-10-08 still confirms the diagram conflict. Current programme-specific OER/implementation rules or university clarification are needed to select between the contradictory current allocations; the older 15-EC choice block is not silently transplanted. Reattempts of the older programme-specific PDF returned a gateway error/timeouts, so its contents are retained as audit-dated evidence and no fresh retrieval is claimed. No unverified component credits are supplied.

exception.reason: The current 2026–2027 official study guide remains internally inconsistent: its diagram gives a 50-EC propedeuse and 135-EC postpropedeuse (185 total), against the 60/120/180 degree description and twelve 5-EC introductory courses in the roster. A programme-specific 2025–2026 OER provides a coherent older 180-EC allocation, but its applicability to the current cohort and changed course roster is unverified. A controlling current programme-specific regulation or university clarification is needed before a 180-EC pathway can be fixed without guessing.
exception.curriculumContext: Current degree: 180 EC, Dutch part-time, four themes and no formal routes. The current guide diagram conflicts with its degree totals and roster. The audit-dated 2025–2026 programme-specific OER gives 60 first-stage + 45 themes + 15 restricted choice + 30 free + 15 skills + 15 graduation = 180; it is prior-year evidence only. Resolve the 2026–2027 curriculum allocation and applicable course membership through current programme-specific rules or university clarification. No unverified components or inferred filler are supplied.
exception.ucrCourseEvidence: Reviewed all 151 course rows of current GitHub main data/reference/ucr_courses_enriched.xlsx. UCR offers substantial related humanities study, for example GOSHIST111 Modern History, GOSHIST112 Histories of Gender, GOSPHIL111 Introduction to Western Philosophy, MCCLITR111 Introduction to Literary Studies, MCCHEAM111 Introduction to Western Art History, MCCHEAM312 Modern Art & Modern Museums, MCCMEDI111 Introduction to Film & Media, MCCMEDI211 From T.V. to TikTok and MCCMEDI311 Media & Race, so a defensible closest-match programme may well exist. The exception rests on the unresolved external curriculum, not on a lack of UCR coverage, and no UCR alternative is encoded.
